title: Viola
summary: A computed viola, outside the real spread: mostly too dark, attacks far too quick, a noisy band near 395 Hz that is the model's. E3 and Gb5 sound 11.2 and 7.3 cents sharp (finger at the equal-tempered station); C4 and Db4 have it moved to the note. Every note is a string with diameters read from photographs of a playing viola, bowed by a finite-width bow with hair compliance on the friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025; C3 on the temperature-dependent row of Smith and Woodhouse 2000 calibrated to it), driving a computed shell body (Cassavetti Stradivari outline; the top plate's interior thickness, the rib height and wall and the back's edge thickness of Stradivari's Gibson viola, the audio-band maple and all 279 modes of its window) and its air cavity at 144 kHz. On every page but C3 and Gb5 the bow force follows bow speed at the start of the stroke (a modelling choice of player move); C4, Db4 and E3 also see the string's omitted bending modes at the bridge and the finger stop (a residual-flexibility record; nothing fitted); G3 and C3 have their after-length moved off the exact sixth by the cello's printed ratio, borrowed. On 11-09 E3, C4, Db4, G3, C3 and D4 took the printed loss of the cello strings of one maker on every string, a stand-in for strings of no stated make (Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, the cello A3, D3, G2 and C2 for the viola's A, D, G and C), in place of the one-string loss from a violin D string that D4 carried on its bowed string and the other pages on their unbowed D string (Q 480, Schoonderwaldt, Guettler and Askenfelt 2008); their loose counts tie on five, rise by one on E3, and the notes move by 3.1 cents at most. Gb5 and A4 kept their pages, because each fell by one on the loose count. Every note also carries three point masses on the shell's rib (the end blocks, a boxwood tailpiece and a Flesch chinrest, 123.3 g, translational only). Every note also carries the viola's other three open strings, unbowed, on the same bridge (the three that are not sounding; on E3, Gb5, C4 and Db4 the sounding string is the one stopped by the finger). E3, Gb5, C4, Db4 and G3 carry a shell-body damping law read from the admittance of a measured viola (Maestre, Scavone and Smith 2013, Fig. 7: 3.4 % at 400 Hz falling as f^-0.41, total damping with the foam holder and damped strings in it, a lower bound on a free viola's Q; weighting alone gives 2.3 to 3.5 %), in place of the violin law (Bissinger 2008: 1.0 % at 400 Hz, f^-0.45) they carried before 11-09; against their live pages their loose counts tie on two, rise by one on E3 and Gb5 and fall by one on C4 and Db4, and the notes move by 0.5 cents at most; the earlier C3, D4, G3 and Db4 renders raised the wood loss 3.25 times instead, a factor with no print above 1 kHz. D4, A4 and C3 radiate through a computed skin instead of the law (3616 triangles over 230 to 1907 Hz, loaded two-way on 68 body modes on the earlier body and on 72 on the new one). C3's loose count ties at 3 of 14 against its law page (strict 2 to 3), so it posts; G3 was tried with the skin too and keeps the law, because its loose count fell from 12 to 11 (its strict count rose from 7 to 9). The rosin's temperature-dependent friction row, tried so far on A4, D4, G3 and C3, raises only C3's loose count (3 to 6 of 14 on the skin page, so C3 takes it); it falls on A4 (8 to 3), D4 (4 to 2) and G3 (12 to 5 on its law card), and those pages keep the isothermal friction law. Every note plays room air from thermochemical data (NASA-9 heat capacities and pure-gas transport) in place of the named-gas row; on D4, A4 and C3 it stacks on the skin. E3, Gb5, C4, Db4, G3, C3, D4 and A4 were re-rendered on 11-08 on a body built from the Gibson viola's printed measurements, the audio-band maple (with the radial loss of Alkadri's plate C) and the whole window of 279 modes, and each page names what got worse first. On 11-09 E3, Gb5, C4 and Db4 also took the string's omitted bending modes at the bow's contact point (the bow-side residual row, admitted beside fixed finger stops since a9c5f2e77); their loose counts tie, and the notes move by 1.6 cents at most. On 11-09 E3, Gb5, C4, Db4, G3, C3, D4 and A4 also took a frozen 20 um oil/copal varnish film on the top and back (the ribs bare, for the engine's projection allowance at 279 modes); their loose counts tie or rise, and the notes move by 0.3 cents at most. On 2026-11-10 C4 and Db4 were restored to earlier renders (deploy 786): C4 plays the 2026-11-09 string-loss page (loose 5 of 14, against 4 for the measured-damping page) and Db4 its 2026-11-06 point-masses page (loose 3, against 1), so the items that list those two notes for the measured body damping, and for Db4 any row added after 11-06, describe renders that are not live. On 2026-11-10 the computed skin was also tried in place of the measured body-damping law on E3, Gb5, C4, Db4 and G3 (and had been on C3): it ties E3 and falls on the others, with the centroid up on three pages and down on three, so it is not posted beyond C3. On 2026-11-10 E3 and G3 were also restored to earlier renders (deploy 793): E3 plays its 2026-11-06 bridge-residual page (loose 11 of 14, strict 9, against 11 and 8 for the measured-damping page) and G3 its 2026-11-09 string-loss page (loose 12, strict 9, against 12 and 7), so the items that list those two notes for a row added after those renders, and for the measured body damping, describe renders that are not live. On 2026-11-10 the rosin's temperature-dependent friction row was also tried on E3, Gb5 and C4 (loose count 11 to 5 of 14, 9 to 9 of 15 with the strict count 8 to 7, and 5 to 2 of 14; harmonics-to-noise 47.6, 47.8 and 66.9 dB against recordings at 33.8, 37.9 and 30.0 dB) and the body-damping row was removed from C4 (5 to 5, total distance 19.03 to 18.37); none is posted. On 2026-11-10 a derived held-damping row (the player's hold, from two held-violin prints) was also tried on C4 (loose 5 and strict 3 of 14, tied with the live page, total distance 19.029 to 19.043), E3 (8 loose and 7 strict of 14 against 11 and 9, total distance 13.939 to 14.079) and Gb5 (8 loose and 7 strict of 15 against 9 and 8, total distance 23.291 to 22.600): not posted.

a computed viola shell body: the outline of the Cassavetti Stradivari viola (Library of Congress), f-holes from its caliper sheet, spruce top and maple back and ribs, a 6.5 mm mesh; the top plate's interior thickness, the rib height and wall and the back's edge thickness from the printed measurements of Stradivari's Gibson viola (Hargrave 1986), the other plate thicknesses from Johannsson's table, the audio-band maple and all 279 modes of the window; the string drives it through bridge flexibility; a 3.24 L air cavity (3.16 L on E3, Gb5, C4, Db4, G3, C3, D4 and A4) through a physical neck (an exterior neck on D4 and A4, whose mouth radiates through the skin below); dry room air (thermochemical on every note); played at 144 kHz on every note
the friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13), on every page but C3 (the thermal row, in the item after the skin item)

strings with diameters measured on a playing viola (Percival 2013, Table 3.2, from photographs, about 10 %), tension and density from Guettler; the bending stiffness is derived from Percival's measured inharmonicity, because no source prints a viola string's stiffness

D4: the string's own loss, from a measurement on another string and carried to this one (DERIVED and BORROWED): loss factors eta_F = eta_B = 1/480 = 2.08e-3, so that every mode has a damping ratio of 1.04e-3, from Table VI of Schoonderwaldt, Guettler and Askenfelt (2008), the D string of a monochord with a rigid termination (decay time of the fundamental 0.521 s, Q1 480; the rigid termination makes the decay the string's own loss; the numbers are from the repository's hand transcription of the table); the viola's open D is the same note. Assumed: only the fundamental was measured, so the loss is constant in mode number; the paper prints Q1 and tau1, not a split between the friction and the bending terms, so the two are equal; the make and core of the viola's D string are unknown. Nothing was set by comparing with a recording. With it the grader scores D4 4 of 14 inside the real-vs-real ruler, as before, and 4 strict against 2; the note starts 442 ms after the bow, against 313 ms before and 604 ms in the recording. On 11-09 this row was replaced on D4, and on the unbowed D string of every page that takes the string loss, by the cello D3's printed pair (the string-loss item below).

Every note: three translational point masses on the shell's rib (on E3, Gb5, C4, Db4, G3, C3, D4 and A4 rebuilt on 11-08 for the Gibson viola's 36.3125 mm rib height in place of Johannsson's 38 mm: end blocks 15.033 g and 13.530 g, 28.930 g with the tailpiece, 123.26 g in all, the same 138, 128 and 32 rib nodes; the figures that follow are the earlier body's), the lumped masses of parts the shell does not model (no lever arm and no rotary inertia, so they cannot show a part's own modes): the upper end block 15.732 g and the lower end block 14.159 g (Johannsson's viola table, Medium: 50 x 18 and 45 x 18 mm by the 38 mm rib height; the table gives no wood, so the shell's own spruce pack at 460 kg/m3 is an assumption), the tailpiece 15.4 g added to the lower block for 29.559 g (Maderas Barber's Hill model boxwood viola tailpiece, 130 mm, ref. 11219; the same maker lists 25 g in ebony and 20 g in French boxwood, so 15 to 25 g, and the one this viola wore is unknown), and a Flesch chinrest of 79.3 g (Luthier Vidal's Wolf KH-21 listing, the only weight found for it; a Goetz Flesch viola chinrest lists 67 g with screws at Thomann), 124.59 g in all. Where they sit is a modelling choice, and no print places them: 138 rib nodes at the top end, 128 at the bottom end, and 32 on the flanks of the lower end block for the chinrest (a Flesch rest is centre-mounted over the tailpiece; a first version that put it off the centre line on the bass side was withdrawn and is on no page). On the earlier body the pole went from one peak at 395.10 Hz, Q 75.3, effective mass 34.0 g to one at 390.76 Hz, Q 73.5, effective mass 41.3 g, and the wave binary reproduces that read (390.76 Hz, Q 73.5, 41.3 g, peak 0.730 m/s/N).
